# Lolajātaka (Ja 274)

**ID:** Ja 274
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Lolajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 In the conclusion (*samodhāna*) of the tale preserved in the edition of Fausböll, the greedy monk is identified as having been a greedy crow (*lolakāko*) who died groaning at the scene, whereas the Bodhisatta was a pigeon (*pārāpato*) who abandoned the dwelling and flew elsewhere; upon hearing the exposition of the four truths, the greedy monk attained the fruit of non-returning (*anāgāmiphala*) [Fausböll 1879].

**Sources**

- [Fausböll 1879] V. Fausböll, Jātaka Together with Its Commentary, Vol. 2 (1879) — Story resolution, identification of the crow and pigeon, attainment of anāgāmiphala, and uddāna vagga placement
